{"id": "d12df139-47fb-4ca1-b241-660f98a25724", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_Ky7aDKUjnLyHUr7Ccv67UQ", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Route model inference requests across AWS Regions with cross-Region inference\",\"context\":\"## Choosing between Geographic and Global cross-Region inference\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock provides two types of cross-Region inference profiles, each designed for\\ndifferent use cases and compliance requirements:\\n\\n| Feature | Geographic Cross-Region Inference | Global Cross-Region Inference | Recommendation |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| Data residency | Within geographic boundaries (such as US, EU, and APAC) | Any supported AWS commercial Region worldwide | Choose Geographic for compliance requirements |\\n| Request routing | Routed within the geography | Routed worldwide | Choose based on where requests can be processed |\\n| Reliability and availability | Routes within the AWS Regions listed in the profile (for example, `us-east-1`, `us-east-2`, and `us-west-2` for a US profile) | Routes across all supported AWS commercial Regions | To meet an availability target, add bounded retries and multi-Region or multi-model fallback in your application. Choose\\nGlobal cross-Region inference when you want cost savings without\\ngeographic restrictions\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cross-region-inference.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Global cross-Region inference\",\"context\":\"## Benefits of global cross-Region inference\\n\\nWith global cross-Region inference, you get the following advantages over a\\ngeographic cross-Region inference profile:\\n\\n* **Cost-efficiency** \u2013 You save approximately\\n 10% on both input and output token pricing compared to geographic\\n cross-Region inference. Even\\n though your requests are processed across different AWS Regions worldwide,\\n you maintain a centralized view of your application's performance and usage\\n patterns through your familiar AWS monitoring tools.\\n* **Worldwide request routing** \u2013 With global\\n cross-Region inference, your requests can be processed by compute across\\n supported commercial AWS Regions worldwide rather than within a single\\n geography\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/global-cross-region-inference.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"#### Amazon Bedrock \u2014 Cross-Region Inference (CRIS)\\n\\n##### Overview\\n\\nCross-region inference (CRIS) profiles let Bedrock route requests across AWS Regions to improve throughput. Two profile types \u2014 Geographic (within US/EU/APAC boundaries) and Global (any commercial Region) \u2014 trade data residency for cost and capacity. There is no additional routing cost; pricing follows the source Region.\\n\\n##### Profile Types\\n\\n| Feature | Geographic | Global |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| **Data residency** | Within geographic boundaries (US, EU, APAC) | Any supported AWS commercial Region worldwide |\\n| **Throughput** | Higher than single-region | Highest available |\\n| **Cost** | Standard pricing | ~10% savings vs. single-region |\\n| **Best suited for** | Organizations with data-residency regulations | Organizations prioritizing cost and performance |\\n\\n##### Operational Details\\n\\n* **No routing cost** \u2014 the request is priced based on the Region from which the inference profile is called.\\n* **Account-level Region enablement is not required for routed Regions** \u2014 cross-region inference can route to Regions that have not been manually enabled in your account.\\n* **Network path** \u2014 all data transmitted during cross-Region operations remains on the AWS network. Traffic never traverses the public internet.\\n* **Encryption in transit** \u2014 data is encrypted between AWS Regions.\\n* **CloudTrail logging** \u2014 all cross-Region inference requests are logged in CloudTrail in your source Region. The additionalEventData.inferenceRegion field shows where each request was actually processed.\\n* **Provisioned Throughput** \u2014 not currently supported through inference profiles\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/gen-ai-inference-architecture-and-best-practices-on-aws/amazon-bedrock.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Regional availability by models\",\"context\":\"## Inference options at a glance\\n\\n| | **In-Region** | **Geographic (Geo) Cross-Region** | **Global Cross-Region** |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| **How it works** | Request is processed entirely within the single AWS Region you specify | Bedrock routes the request to a Region within a defined geography (US, CA, EU, APAC, JP, AU, IN) | Bedrock routes the request to any supported commercial Region worldwide |\\n| **Data residency** | Strictly within one Region | Within geographic boundaries (e.g., all EU Regions); prompts and outputs may move within the geography but not outside it | No geographic restrictions; data may be processed in any commercial Region |\\n| **Request routing** | Processed in the Region you specify; subject to per-Region service quotas | Routed to a Region within the geography | Routed to a supported commercial Region worldwide |\\n| **Pricing** | Standard on-demand pricing for that Region | Priced at source Region rates; no surcharge for cross-Region routing | Priced at source Region rates; no surcharge for cross-Region routing. For some models, the per-token price is lower than geographic cross-Region inference |\\n| **modelId format** | Direct model ID: `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0` | Geography prefix + model ID: `us.anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0` | Global prefix + model ID: `global.anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0` |\\n| **Best for** | Strict single-Region compliance; Provisioned Throughput workloads | Data residency regulations scoped to a geography (e.g., GDPR in EU, data sovereignty requirements) | Cost efficiency with no data residency constraints |\\n\\nNow, let us look at Regional availability across all the models supported by Amazon Bedrock\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-region-compatibility.html\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"What's New at AWS - Cloud Innovation & News\",\"context\":\"Amazon Bedrock, a service for building generative AI applications and agents, now supports Global cross-Region inference for Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4 model. Previously, users could only choose cross-region inference profiles tied to specific geographies, which automatically selected the optimal region within that geography. With the new Global cross-region inference profile, users can distribute traffic across multiple AWS Regions, enabling higher throughput for generative AI use cases that do not require a specific geography. The documentation provides information on increasing throughput with cross-region inference, supported regions and models for inference profiles, and steps to use an inference profile in model invocation. This feature is designed to help manage unplanned traffic bursts and optimize resources during peak usage times\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/09/amazon-bedrock-global-cross-region-inference-anthropic-claude-sonnet-4/\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up Bedrock global vs US inference profile pricing"}

{"id": "05805751-e1e0-4f68-aef5-f212dfecdeeb", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Switching should cut your Claude Sonnet 5 bill by about 10%. I couldn't confirm that from this account's data, and there are a few things to check before you switch.

**Savings**
- AWS documents global cross-Region inference as roughly 10% cheaper than geographic profiles on both input and output tokens. Geographic profiles are billed at standard pricing.
- Pricing follows the Region you call from, which is us-east-1 for you. There is no routing surcharge.
- The documentation says "approximately 10%" and doesn't give a per-model figure. Another page says only "for some models" the global price is lower. Check the Bedrock pricing page for Sonnet 5's exact global and US rates before you commit to a number.
- The saving applies only to Sonnet 5 token spend. Guardrails, other models and any cache pricing aren't covered by this figure.

**What I found in this account (012345678901_1)**
- **Both profiles exist and are active:** `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` and `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`. Switching means changing the model ID in your callers.
- **No Sonnet 5 spend shows up here.** Over the last 30 days, Cost Explorer shows only Nova Lite, Titan embeddings, Guardrails and a few small models. Nova Lite is the largest at about $0.79 this month. So I can't give you a dollar figure from this account. If your Sonnet 5 traffic runs in another account, apply the ~10% to that account's Sonnet 5 line item.
- **Invocation logging is on**, writing to the `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations` log group. CloudTrail and CloudWatch keep logging in your source Region even when requests are processed elsewhere. That log group is the place to measure your real Sonnet 5 token volume.
- **The one custom inference profile** (`llmops-lf-aip-team-a`) wraps Nova Lite, not Sonnet. It isn't affected.

**What to confirm before switching**
